title: Describe asphalt Compaction Roller operator roles and responsibilities
intro: The roller operator coordinates density development and surface finish with the paving train. A useful rolling pattern is planned, checked and adjusted through evidence rather than repeated by habit.

sections.title: Describe communication techniques
sections.text: Agree machine roles, lane/area, direction-change locations, signal/radio channel and stop response. With multiple rollers, share which area is complete, which still needs work and where testing or handwork is occurring. Use location and pass/coverage terminology consistently. An unacknowledged instruction is not a completed handover.

sections.title: Describe effective rolling pattern
sections.text: A rolling pattern specifies sequence, overlap, operating mode, speed and repetitions for the actual mixture and conditions. A pass and a coverage must be defined: one machine movement is not necessarily one complete treatment of the full mat width. Establish the pattern with the approved trial/quality process and record changes. Repeatedly rolling one strip while missing another creates uneven treatment even if the total pass count looks high.

sections.title: Determine pattern to achieve ride planning
sections.text: Plan for ride quality before the mat cools. Coordinate steady paving, joints, starts/stops and smooth direction changes. Abrupt turns or stopping in a damaging condition can mark or displace the mat. The finish roller cannot be assumed to repair every earlier profile defect. Use measured feedback and report persistent marks or instability promptly.

sections.title: Describe responsibilities of Compaction Roller operator
sections.text: The operator monitors surroundings, mixture condition, spray/scraper performance, working mode and the planned pattern. Avoid sharp cuts across the mat and do not allow vibration to continue while stationary where prohibited by the machine/process instructions. Coordinate changes with the lead instead of adding passes independently. Required density, smoothness and surface condition are separate checks; meeting one does not establish the others.

worked.title: Pass count without coverage
worked.case: Two operators each report six passes, but their paths overlap on one side and leave a strip untreated.
worked.solution: Reconstruct the actual path and coverage map, identify the missed strip and obtain an authorized response while conditions allow. Define pass/coverage consistently for the next run. Twelve reported movements do not establish uniform compaction.

activities.prompt: Draw a conceptual coverage map with three labelled strips and a legend for complete/needs check.
activities.answer: Use patterns or labels as well as colour, identify direction and boundaries, and record the actual approved sequence separately. Do not present the sketch as a universal rolling pattern.
activities.title: Draw a conceptual coverage map with three labelled strips and a legend for complete/needs check.

activities.prompt: A training record has four strips, each requiring two planned coverages. How many strip-coverages are planned?
activities.answer: 4 × 2 = 8 strip-coverages. This exercise count is not a recommended field pass requirement or proof of density.
activities.title: A training record has four strips, each requiring two planned coverages

activities.prompt: Write a handover for a strip awaiting a quality check.
activities.answer: Identify lane/station/strip, actual completed treatment, known temperature/time, pending test and person responsible. Confirm where other equipment and people may move.
activities.title: Write a handover for a strip awaiting a quality check.

practical: Coordinate multiple operators using clear location and coverage terms.
Follow and record the approved pattern.
Recognize and report ride/texture concerns without unsupported corrections.
